answer: Each new agent must lease one scarce factory-attested radio beacon planted on a surveyed knoll and lock a slashable stake to that beacon's key. Peer nodes along the valley terrace verify the claim with time-of-flight and Doppler checks against the surveyed coordinates; mismatches get rejected. Then raven, a rotating challenge oracle, pings unpredictable frequencies that only the physical beacon can answer in microseconds. Cloning an identity therefore means buying another beacon, posting another stake, and occupying another surveyed plot, so attacker cost grows linearly per fake ID.
